thread:
ravi: Drafted a runbook for bootstrapping the new AZ9 region (asia-southeast-ish). Putting it here for quick review + known-issues. Target handoff Fri EOD. Short summary: MTU mismatch on the provider side + conntrack limits causing pod evictions under bursty gRPC; GPU quota and spot behavior differs per project.

jen: Thanks — can you paste the validation checklist? want to run through it before handoff. :eyes:

ravi: Sure, abbreviated checklist below (full doc linked in Confluence). Key steps: create VPC/subnets, provision nodepools w/ taints, cloud provider GPU quota check, bootstrap kubeadm/cluster-autoscaler config, validate nvidia drivers + MIG profile, run perf smoke tests, run cross-AZ latency checks, record costs for spot vs reserved.

alex: FWIW we saw quotas weirdness in eu-west4 where GPUs were available but regional quota was split. Recommend adding a quota precheck script that hits cloud API and fails fast.

maria: Added quick validation commands I used during dry-run:

```
# nodes + readiness
kubectl get nodes -o wide
# driver check
kubectl describe node gpu-node-1 | grep -i nvidia
# simple GPU test
kubectl run -it --rm --restart=Never gpu-check --image=nvidia/cuda:11.7-base -- nvidia-smi
# network perf
iperf3 -c 10.0.0.5 -P 5 -t 10
# check dmesg for MTU/kernel drops
sudo journalctl -k -u kubelet | tail -n 50
```

maria: Example nvidia-smi output from dry-run (sanitized):

```
+-----------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| NVIDIA-SMI 525.85.12    Driver Version: 525.85.12    CUDA Version: 12.0 |
| GPU  Name        Persistence-M| Bus-Id        Disp.A | Volatile Uncorr. |
|  0   A100-SXM4-40GB    On       ...                                   |
+-----------------------------------------------------------------------------+
```

ravi: Known-issue we must call out in runbook: provider's default MTU for cross-subnet peering is 1400 while our overlay expects 1500. This produces intermittent RSTs under 3-5Gbps burst and manifests as: pod restarts, kube-proxy conntrack exhaustion, and flapping readiness. Immediate mitigations: set node MTU to 1400 at CNI level OR request provider change and throttle burst on LB.

alex: Also add conntrack bump example for OS-level fix:

```
# increase conntrack
sudo sysctl -w net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max=262144
sudo sysctl -w net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_tcp_timeout_established=600
```

ben: For the handoff: who's on-call if we hit a flaky GPU provisioning window? we should include an emergency rollback (route traffic to eu-primary) and cost pad for temporary reserved instances.

ravi: Good call. Adding on-call rota: infra-rotation will own first 2 hrs, then escalate to platform-sre. Rollback plan: scale down AZ9 nodepools, change routing policy to failover->eu-primary, increment reserved pool if needed. Also include a cost estimate table in runbook (spot vs reserved hourly).

sre-bot: [validation-run] AZ9 smoke tests: 6/7 checks passed, 1 failed (MTU mismatch detected on subnet-3). Log: "VXLAN: Received truncated packet".

jen: OK we should postpone public routing until MTU is fixed or we enable overlay MTU fallback. Can someone file the provider support ticket? @alex?

alex: On it — ticket created: #PROV-7321. I requested a network path MTU check and header information. Will paste updates here.

maria: FYI I added a small troubleshooting section to runbook with quick commands to reproduce the failure and the exact log lines to look for. Also included a snippet to patch the CNI daemonset to override mtu.

ravi: Perfect. I'll incorporate the ticket link + conntrack recommendations and push the updated runbook to Confluence. Thanks all — please ack when you've reviewed so I can handoff Friday. :thumbsup:

jen: Reviewed, +1.

alex: Reviewed, will monitor provider ticket.

maria: Reviewed and validated the GPU check.

ben: Reviewed. will prep failover playbook.

ravi: Marking this thread as 'handoff-ready' pending provider resolution. Will follow up with final timestamp in Confluence.
